text:
Title: Marks that lag, spreads that don't

Rating: underweight

Grimshaw Partners, 2028-03-15. The data panel is not subtle, though the marks pretend otherwise. Private credit shows a one_year_return of +3.3% even as ytd_return sits at -12.0% — a divergence that only makes sense if one assumes valuation committees are still working off a stale quarter.¹ The reported_vs_public_gap of +9.5% is the tell: public proxies have already repriced for a world of hy_spread_now_bps at 780bps, while private books have not yet caught up. Lagging marks are not the same as stable value.

Calder & Root's view — that policy support resolves the stress — asks us to believe policy_rate_now at 5.25% is doing more work than the newsflow suggests. Equities entering bear market territory and spreads gapping wider on default fears are not symptoms that yield readily to rate relief; they are symptoms of credit quality reassertion, the kind that outlasts a policy pivot narrative. Cpi_now at 4.1% keeps the central bank's hands somewhat tied besides, which undercuts the "support resolves it" thesis at the root.

Picture, if you will, a chart with two lines: the private_credit NAV index, smooth and gently declining, sitting atop a public high-yield index that has just fallen off a shelf. The gap between them is not evidence of resilience; it is evidence of a lag waiting to close, likely downward, once drawdown of -18.0% forces recognition events across the book.

The risk to this view: if policy easing does arrive credibly and default fears prove overstated, the reported_vs_public_gap could close upward instead — marks catching up to a public recovery rather than a public rout. That scenario would make the cautious read look merely early rather than correct.

¹ Valuation committees rarely mark faster than they must.
